elements.title: Figure 14.—Relation Between Byproduct Elements and Host Metals
elements.content:
Chart kind: Radial circular chart
Axes: Radial distance from center representing percentage of primary production originating with host metal (0% to 100%)
Legend/Explanation: Principal host metals in inner circle; byproduct elements in outer circle at distances proportional to percentage of production originating with host metal; companion elements in white region of outer circle with undetermined percentage.
Inner circle (host metals): Au, Al, Ti, Fe, Ni, Cu, Zn, Pb, Sn, Pt
Outer circle byproduct elements arranged radially around each host metal with approximate percentage distances:
- Au: Ag, Cu, Cr, Ni, Co
- Al: Ga, Zr, Hf
- Ti: V, Y, La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Ho, Dy, Er, Tm, Yb, Lu
- Fe: Th, Fe
- Ni: Mn, Tb, Dy, Gd, Sm, Y
- Cu: Co, Pd, Te, Se
- Zn: Cd, In, Ge, Ag
- Pb: Bi, Sb, As, Hg
- Sn: Rh, Ru, Os, Ir
- Pt: Pd
White region companion elements (undetermined %): Ba, As, Sb, U, Hg, Cu, Zn, Ag, Cu, As, Er, Ho, Dy, Tb, Gd, Eu, Sm, Nd, Pr, Ce, La, Y, Tl, Se, Ba, Pb, Sn, Au, U, Fe, Hg, Tl, Bi, In, Sn, Zn, Pb, As, Ba
Notes: Full element names and abbreviations listed below chart. Source: Nassar, N.T., Graedel, T.E., and Harper, E.M., 2015, By-product metals are technologically essential but have problematic supply: Science Advances, v. 1, no. 3, article E1400180. (Accessed January 19, 2023, at https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.1400180.)
